The failing byte 0xFA (250 decimal) falls in Windows-31J extension range (0xFA-0xFC) not handled by original decoder. Production fix adds: (1) 768 character mappings (0xED40-0xEEFC, 0xFA40-0xFC4B) covering Windows-31J-specific kanji, (2) conditional branch in jis.dart to decode 0xFA-0xFC range. Strict validation confirms both tests reproduce on buggy revision and pass on fixed revision with deterministic fingerprints across 3 repetitions.

This is a legitimate character encoding defect in a Dart Shift-JIS/Windows-31J decoder. Issue #5 reports concrete failure: input bytes [142, 82, 250, 177, 32, 149, 113, 142, 247] decode incorrectly to '山�ｱ 敏樹' instead of expected '山﨑 敏樹'. The byte 0xFA (250 decimal) falls in the Windows-31J extension range (0xFA-0xFC) not covered by the original JIS X 0208 decoder. The production fix adds exactly two changes: (1) 768 character mappings for Windows-31J-specific codes 0xED40-0xFC4B in jis-table.dart, and (2) a 4-line conditional branch in jis.dart to decode the 0xFA-0xFC range. The trigger tests directly validate the reported bug with exact input bytes and add comprehensive roundtrip testing for ~600 Windows-31J characters. Runtime evidence confirms both triggers fail deterministically on buggy and pass on fixed. No unrelated formatting, documentation, or feature work is present. The active_same_project_root_causes list is empty, confirming no duplicate.
